ratings_why.fun: Whom-am-I-on is a clear, satisfying question every turn, and watching one buff ripple down a tree is a real growth payoff; the chain arithmetic is the cost.
ratings_why.distinct: Copying a host's gains and blooming on a small host play unlike any of today's tribes, though the host buffers themselves are familiar.

verdict_why: Mistletoe Clump's wording and the triple rule for vines are real reading gaps; both are small wording fixes.

points.text: Mistletoe Clump's "gain +1/+1, and take 1/1 from its host" reads as +2/+2 in total or as a 1/1 move; the tier note says a move. Say "permanently take 1/1 from its host".
Climb doesn't say what happens to vines when a climber or host becomes golden in a triple, which players will hit often. Put the proposed rule (its climbers fall) in the Climb text.
Start of Combat buffs (Twiner, Ivy in Flower, Viscum) ripple down chains at half, at least 1, which nobody can add up at a glance. Show each unit's after-cascade stats in the recruit preview.
Dodder Thread on an enemy also copies that enemy's fight gains, by the Climb rule. That is the best gatecrasher moment; say it on the card.
Lady Hedera's card should say a second copy does nothing, as the risks note suggests, so a player doesn't buy one expecting double.

standouts.why: Dodder Thread leaving its host to drink from the enemy for the fight is the parasite fantasy in pure play.
Ruin Ivy holding its host up with Damage Reduction is the ivy-clad ruin, and Bloom reads in one line.
Old Man's Beard turns a dead host into an inheritance; one clear trigger, and it reads as the hermit who outlives everyone.

weakest.why: Barley-sugar Twiner is a plain Start of Combat host buff; the tight honeysuckle twist doesn't show in what it does.
Hanger-on's two conditions for flat gold are a lot to check each turn for a small payout.
Viscum's old blood reads as a generic count-based team buff, and counting bloomers is extra work at Start of Combat.

flags.note: Gain and take may be read as two separate gains.
Full share down every chain plus re-climbing the biggest unit each turn could make one tree huge fast.
A large early host death can hand five climbers huge stats in one fight, as the risks note says.
